summary: Close the Connector SDK security/runtime boundary with a reusable no-skip conformance harness, machine-readable passing evidence, Linux reference qualification, and future provider-admission enforcement without admitting a provider in the Task-064 completion change.

impacts.evidence: The mandatory tenant-isolation check exercises own-tenant success and foreign-tenant denial through a provider conformance adapter; no global tenant authority or database bypass is introduced.

Conformance reports contain only connector identity, ordered outcomes, bounded reason codes, timestamps and hashes; raw provider bodies, credentials, PII and arbitrary error strings are not report fields.
Task 064 adds one Draft 2020-12 conformance-report schema and a new Connector SDK subpackage without changing existing public API, event, webhook, manifest, sandbox or SDK-root contracts.
No EventBus event type or event payload is added or modified by the conformance harness.

Providers gain an additive conformance Candidate adapter and report contract under the already approved internal/platform/connectors SDK prefix; Connector, Runtime and SecretAccessor v1 root interfaces remain unchanged.
Task 064 adds no PostgreSQL table, column, constraint or migration; provider inventory remains empty.

The required suite proves production-credential rejection, dry-run side-effect suppression, egress grants, normalized failure reporting, resource-limit failure and Task-029 Linux environment/filesystem/direct-network isolation.
The harness does not authorize sensitive production writes or bypass Task-017 approval policy; it only certifies connector boundary behavior before provider admission.
The machine report carries stable connector/version identity, ordered check results and a SHA-256 mutation detector suitable for release evidence while excluding raw provider response content.
A mandatory repeated-write probe requires one applied effect followed by a duplicate-safe replay with the identical effect fingerprint; reconciliation semantics remain owned by Task 014.
Mandatory webhook replay/deduplication and Task-029 exact egress allow/deny checks are included; Task 063 still owns durable outbound webhook delivery, signing, retries and replay history.
Conformance exposes deterministic normalized check outcomes and verifies bounded retry/resource behavior; it adds no production telemetry backend.
Rollback removes the additive harness/report enforcement with no data migration. Provider admission remains disabled in this change, so rollback cannot strand an admitted provider.

Thirteen mandatory no-skip checks, strict report validation, negative mutation/isolation tests and a real Linux reference qualification are added to repository checks and future provider admission evidence.
